title: Every Node Wants the Crown
prompt:
**Scenario.** Tree, n ≤ 200000: for every vertex, the sum of distances to all others. What is the intended technique?

**Which approach is the best fit? The program only needs to print the letter.**

**A)** Run BFS from every vertex — O(n²) but constants are small

**B)** One post-order DP for subtree contributions, then one pre-order reroot pass with an O(1) exchange per edge

**C)** Floyd–Warshall on the tree

**D)** Binary lifting to LCA, then sum pairwise distances

tests.name: answer
tests.hint: The classic reroot: two linear passes with the exchange formula. O(n²) dies at 200000; Floyd is nonsense on trees; pairwise LCA sums are O(n²).
